name: Airbnb
look: Photography-first marketplace on 90% white, one Rausch accent used scarcely, a pill search bar and a single elevation tier.

hero.title: Not just a place to stay. A place to be.
hero.sub: Seven million homes, hosted by people who live there. Book a whole house, a spare room, or a boat moored in a harbour you have never heard of.

features.title: Booked by people, hosted by people
features.sub: Every listing has someone behind it who has answered a message at eleven at night.

items.title: Whole homes
items.body: Not a hotel room with a kitchenette. An actual house, with a kettle that belongs to someone and a note about the bins.

items.title: Guest favourite
items.body: A badge only given to listings in the top ten percent by rating, reliability and how often the host answers.

items.title: Real hosts
items.body: Median first reply is eleven minutes. Response rate and time are shown on every profile, not just the good ones.

items.title: Flexible cancellation
items.body: Filter by cancellation policy before you search, so you are not reading small print at checkout.

items.title: Neighbourhood notes
items.body: Written by the host, about the actual street — where the bread is good and which door sticks.

items.title: The price is the price
items.body: Cleaning and service fees are in the headline number from the first search result. No reveal at checkout.

showcases.title: The top ten percent, and why
showcases.body: A listing earns the badge on rating, cancellation history and response rate together — not on reviews alone. The three components are shown on the listing, so you can see which one carried it.
points: Recalculated monthly, and can be lost

showcases.title: Hosting, without guessing
showcases.body: Set a nightly rate and the dashboard shows what comparable homes nearby actually charged last month, with occupancy. You keep control of the price; you just stop guessing at it.
points: Occupancy by week for your area
Payouts released the morning after check-in

gallery.title: Places people are booking
gallery.sub: A selection from this week, across five continents.

testimonial.quote: The host left a hand-drawn map of which bakery opens on a Sunday. I have stayed in hotels that cost four times as much and remembered none of them.
testimonial.name: Sofia Marchetti

pricing.title: Hosting on Wayfare
pricing.sub: Free to list. You are charged only when someone actually books.

tiers.name: Standard
tiers.desc: For hosts with one or two places.

items.q: Are fees included in the price I see?
items.a: Yes. Cleaning and service fees are in the headline number from the first search result onwards, so the total at checkout is the number you have been looking at all along.
It is set per listing and shown as a filter before you search. Flexible allows free cancellation up to 24 hours before check-in; the stricter tiers are labelled plainly on the listing.
Hosts are covered up to three million per booking. Claims are filed through the resolution centre with photographs, and the guest is contacted before anything is charged.
The morning after check-in, to the account on file. Longer stays are paid monthly rather than in a lump at the end.

cta.title: Find somewhere worth staying
cta.sub: Seven million homes, and every one of them has someone behind it.

footer.tagline: A marketplace for places people actually live in.

notes: One accent — Rausch — carries every primary CTA, the search orb and the save state. Most of the page is white and ink with one or two Rausch moments.
Display weights sit at 500–700 and body at 400. The modest weight is deliberate: the system trusts photography for visual heft.
The global search is a fully-rounded white pill divided by 1px hairlines into segments, terminated by a circular accent orb.
Property cards are photo-first — a clipped aspect-ratio image, a floating badge top-left, a heart top-right, then four or five lines of meta.
Elevation caps at a single shadow tier used on hover-floated cards and dropdowns. Footer and language menus are plain text columns with no card surface at all.
